description: A clock divider on one side, a clock counter or clock delay on the other, and a fourth output that combines the two

params.text: Sets the division: 1, then every even number up to 64
In the counting setting, sets how many clocks pass between pulses, 1 to 32; in the delay setting, sets the delay, 0 to 1000ms; in the off setting it does nothing
Sets how much of the division CV reaches the division knob, none at the far left and the whole of its travel at the far right
Sets how much of the count-or-delay CV reaches that knob, none at the far left and the whole of its travel at the far right
Chooses what the right-hand side does: count clocks, delay them, or nothing, and in the off setting the division, count and combined outputs are all held at 0V

inputs.text: Adds to the division knob, 10V covering the whole of its travel at full attenuation
Adds to the count-or-delay knob, 10V covering the whole of its travel at full attenuation
A rising edge past 1V restarts the divider, the counter and the delay together
Advances the divider, the counter and the delay on each rising edge past 1V

outputs.text: A square wave at the divided rate, flipping between 0V and 10V each time the division count comes round; set to 1 it repeats the clock instead of halving it
In the counting setting, 10V for one clock each time the count comes round; in the delay setting, the clock pulse repeated after the set delay
In the counting setting, a pulse once the counter has counted that many of the divider's changes; in the delay setting, the clock with pulses landing on a divider change pushed late, giving a swing
Carries 10V for as long as the clock input is above its threshold and 0V below it

notes: nothing moves until a clock is patched; the module has no clock of its own
the delay is worked out in blocks of 64 samples rather than one sample at a time, so the delayed edge lands to the nearest block

inputs.0:
±10V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 10V.
inputs.1:
±10V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 10V.
inputs.2:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.3:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage does nothing here.
